## Toolkit

- **P2 — Queue draining can prevent shutdown from completing.** [rpc.cc:565](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/ironweave/src/rpc/rpc.cc:565): An accepted compressor frame can be blocked in a direct socket write while the peer stays connected without reading. The new wait delays socket shutdown until that write finishes. Previously, closing an empty local output buffer could reach `SHUT_WR` and release the blocked write. Without an independent disconnect or abort, stream closure can now wait indefinitely.

- **P2 — The new sink breaks older supported API configurations.** [rpc_test.cc:1883](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/ironweave/tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:1883): With `Seastar_API_LEVEL=7` or `8`, `data_sink_impl` requires `put(net::packet)`. The unconditional span overload does not override that interface, leaving the helper abstract and preventing `rpc_test` from compiling.

- **P2 — The reproducer can pass without exercising the new guard.** [rpc_test.cc:2017](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/ironweave/tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2017): The peer can consume EOF and close its socket before the hook runs, causing the client receive loop to set `_error`. The existing rejection then satisfies the test even with `_stream_closing` rejection removed. Parking local sink closure does not exclude this ordering.

- **P2 — Successful silent rejection also passes.** [rpc_test.cc:2016](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/ironweave/tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2016): The test catches `closed_error` but accepts normal completion. Returning success while discarding the frame therefore passes, despite violating the promised exceptional result.

- **P2 — The close-entry wait has no local failure bound.** [rpc_test.cc:2011](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/ironweave/tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2011): If the expected close transition is not reached, this wait prevents release and cleanup from running. Only the external test timeout—300 seconds by default—bounds the failure.

- **P2 — A failed assertion bypasses required cleanup.** [rpc_test.cc:2000](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/ironweave/tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2000): Failure of the hook-count assertion unwinds an unclosed sink. Its destructor asserts `sink_closed()`, potentially aborting the runner instead of reporting the assertion failure. Enclosing client cleanup runs after these local handles unwind.

## Standards

- **P3 — “Pass-through compressor” inaccurately describes the helper.** [rpc_test.cc:1937](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/ironweave/tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:1937): The helper performs LZ4 compression with chunk headers and additionally substitutes the empty-buffer representation. It preserves decoded content, but does not pass through the input bytes.

## Spec

- **P2 — A decoding exception does not close the source.** [rpc_types.hh:387](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/ironweave/include/seastar/rpc/rpc_types.hh:387), also [rpc-streaming.md:111](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/ironweave/doc/rpc-streaming.md:111): The new documentation says reading until the source throws closes it. However, exceptions from `unmarshall()` escape without calling `close_source()`; only receive failures and EOF perform that transition. Following the documented contract after a decoding exception can leave the connection open. This is newly incorrect documentation of existing behavior.

Coverage limitations: Doxygen anchor resolution and all timing constraints on `suspend_for_testing()` remain unverified. Tests were not run. HEAD remained pinned and the worktree clean.

  "body": "`connection::stream_close()` closes the connection's write buffer while `_error` is still false; `_error` is only set by the `stop()` it runs afterwards. In between, `connection::send()` keeps accepting frames. Sinks cannot send at that point, but the `send_empty_frame` hook handed to every negotiated compressor is `[this] { return send({}); }` and is not guarded, and a compressor may call it at any time. Scylla's does whenever a new compression dictionary is announced, on every connection on the shard at once.

A frame accepted in that window is written into the closed `output_stream` and `flush()`ed, which registers a batch flush that nothing waits for or closes: `stream_close()` has moved on, and `stop_send_loop()` skips `write_buf.close()` because `_sink_closed_future` already reports the buffer closed. The loop then ends, the application drops its sink and source as it is entitled to, and the connection is destroyed with the flush still pending:

```
seastar::output_stream<char>::~output_stream(): Assertion `!_in_batch && "Was this stream properly closed?"' failed.
```

This is what two Scylla nodes hit during tablet streaming. The core dump shows the same 141-byte compressor control frame sitting unflushed on both the stream connection being destroyed and on its parent client, with the stream fully closed and its loop already over.

The fix marks the connection as closing in `stream_close()` before the write buffer is touched, and `send()` fails with `closed_error` from then on. Frames that `send()` accepted just before the mark may still be queued, so `stream_close()` also waits for `_outgoing_queue` to drain, by chaining on `_outgoing_queue_ready` the way `send()` does, before it closes the buffer. Setting `_error` there instead is not an option: `stop()` would then skip the `shutdown_input()` that wakes the receive loop, and `stop_send_loop()` would `shutdown_output()` before the eof marker written by this very close reaches the peer.

The series:

1. the fix;
2. a deterministic reproducer: the stream socket's `data_sink::close()` is parked, the captured `send_empty_frame` hook is fired while it is parked, and any `put()` after `close()` is recorded. Without the fix it fails on the recorded write; leaving the late `put()` unresolved instead reproduces the exact assertion above;
3. documentation of the stream shutdown contract (close the sink, drain the source to eof or error), which was nowhere written down, and a correction of the sentence in `doc/rpc-streaming.md` that read as if closing the client were a substitute.

Only the first two commits are needed for a backport.

      "messageBody": "connection::stream_close() closes the connection's write buffer while
_error is still false.  _error is only set by the stop() it runs
afterwards, and in between connection::send() keeps accepting frames.
Nothing is supposed to send at that point, and the sinks indeed cannot:
sink_impl::send_buffer() checks sink_closed().  But the send_empty_frame
hook handed to every negotiated compressor is `[this] { return send({}); }`
and is not guarded, and a compressor may call it at any time -- Scylla's
does whenever a new compression dictionary is announced, on every
connection on the shard at once.

A frame accepted in that window is written into the closed output_stream
and flush()ed, which registers it for a batch flush that nothing waits
for or closes: stream_close() has moved on, and stop_send_loop() skips
its own write_buf.close() because _sink_closed_future already reports
that the buffer was closed by stream_close().  The loop then ends, the
application drops its sink and source as it is entitled to, and the
connection is destroyed with the flush still pending:

  seastar::output_stream<char>::~output_stream(): Assertion `!_in_batch
  && "Was this stream properly closed?"' failed.

That is the crash a Scylla node hit during tablet streaming, with the
same 141-byte compressor control frame sitting unflushed on both the
stream connection being destroyed and its parent client.  Without the
assertion the flush poller would run on freed memory.

Mark the connection as closing in stream_close() before the write buffer
is touched and have send() fail with closed_error from then on, the same
way it does once _error is set.  A frame that send() accepted just
before the mark may still be sitting in _outgoing_queue, waiting for its
turn, so also wait for the queue to drain before closing the buffer, by
waiting for _outgoing_queue_ready: by construction it resolves once the
last accepted entry has been written and flushed into the batch the
close then covers.

Setting _error itself in stream_close() is not an option: stop() would
then find it already set and skip the shutdown_input() that wakes the
receive loop, and stop_send_loop() would shutdown_output() before the
eof marker written by this very close has reached the peer.

Fixes #3663

parks until the test releases it and any put() that arrives after close()
was entered is recorded.  A pass-through compressor hands the test the
send_empty_frame hook rpc gives it.  The peer closes its sink first, so
the client's later sink.close() is what runs stream_close() and closes
the write buffer.  While that close is parked the test calls the stream
compressor's hook.

Without the fix the hook's frame is written into the closed output
stream and the test fails on the recorded write.  Had the write been
left in flight instead of completing, dropping the sink and source at
the end would trip ~output_stream()'s `!_in_batch` assertion -- the
exact failure seen in the field; verified by temporarily making the late
put() never resolve.  With the fix the hook fails with closed_error and
nothing is written.

      "messageBody": "Shutting a stream down has a contract that was nowhere written down.
Both halves have to be closed: the sink via close(), the source by
reading it to eof or error, since rpc::source deliberately has no
close(). Only once both are closed does stream_close() run and wait for
the connection's loop to stop. Close one half alone and nothing waits
for the connection, and it is never shut down.

Until now the only trace of any of this was the SEASTAR_ASSERT in
~sink_impl, which covers the sink half only; abandoning a source fails
silently. doc/rpc-streaming.md said nothing about it, and what it did
say about teardown was misleading: "the stream will be aborted if the
client is closed before streaming is" reads as a sanctioned way to
abandon a stream that never reaches eof, which it is not -- dropping the
unclosed sink afterwards still asserts.

Write the contract down in doc/rpc-streaming.md, correct that sentence,
and put it on rpc::sink and rpc::source themselves, where someone
reaching for the API will see it.

Documentation only, no functional change.
